title: Lamb Manti with Garlic Yogurt

items.raw: 2½ cups (320 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
½ cup (120 ml) water, plus 1–2 tablespoons as needed
1 small onion, grated and squeezed dry
½ teaspoon salt, ¼ teaspoon black pepper, ½ teaspoon Aleppo pepper
2 cups whole-milk Greek yogurt, at room temperature, with 2 garlic cloves grated and a pinch of salt
4 tablespoons butter, 1 tablespoon Aleppo pepper or 2 teaspoons paprika, 1 teaspoon tomato paste
Dried mint and sumac, to finish

steps.text: Mix the flour and salt in a bowl, add the egg and water, and stir into a shaggy dough. Knead 8 minutes until smooth and firm; add water a teaspoon at a time if dry. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Knead the lamb, grated onion, parsley, salt, and peppers together with your hands until sticky and uniform.
Divide the dough in half. On a floured counter, roll each half into a very thin sheet, about 1/16 inch — thin enough to see the counter through it. Cut into 1½-inch squares.

Put a chickpea-sized ball of filling in the center of each square. Bring the four corners up to the center and pinch them together, then pinch the four seams closed, making a small four-pointed pouch. Set on a floured tray.
Melt the butter in a small pan, stir in the Aleppo pepper and tomato paste, and cook 1 minute until sizzling and red. Keep warm.
Boil the manti in a large pot of salted water, stirring gently, until the dough is tender and the filling cooked, 8 to 10 minutes after they float. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Spread the garlic yogurt on warm plates, pile the manti on top, and spoon the red butter over. Finish with a pinch of dried mint and sumac.

notes.label: Smaller is traditional
notes.text: the old test is that a spoonful should hold many manti. Do not worry about perfection; the yogurt hides everything.

notes.label: Freezing
notes.text: freeze uncooked manti on the floured tray, then bag them, for 2 months. Cook from frozen, adding a few minutes.

notes.label: Room-temperature yogurt
notes.text: cold yogurt against hot dumplings makes the dish lukewarm. Take it out an hour ahead.

notes.label: Shortcut
notes.text: square wonton wrappers, cut into quarters, work in a pinch.

openQuestion: Who makes the manti, and when? Is your version Turkish — tiny boiled dumplings with yogurt and red-pepper butter — or another style, larger and steamed?
